Checks the account and plans to call the IRS

snippet: A person received a letter claiming to be from the IRS about a refund owed from 2020. They checked their account and planned to call to verify it.

events.detail: Met on a dating app and shared personal details
Claims to be an IRS officer with an MBBS degree
Shares degree, ID and passport images over video call
Finds the rank claim inconsistent and communication secretive

snippet: A woman met a man on a dating app who claimed to be an IRS officer and shared identity documents. She became suspicious after finding inconsistencies in his claims and secretive communication.

events.detail: Bank letter demands an IRS form with SSN or higher withholding
Notices no stamped envelope and calls the bank's fraud team
Disregards the letter after the bank says it is not genuine

snippet: A bank customer received a letter demanding an IRS form with their Social Security number. They called the bank's fraud team, which said the letter was not genuine.

events.detail: WhatsApp contact says he is moving to the victim's area
Chats for a year and pitches crypto-linked investments
Pressures the victim to open an IRS account immediately
Asks what the purpose of the IRS account is

snippet: A person chatted with a WhatsApp contact for a year, who pitched crypto investments and then pressed them to open an IRS account immediately. They asked what the purpose was.

events.detail: Facebook contact poses as a military sergeant
Builds a bond over WhatsApp with a shared backstory
Sends a fake IRS document to prove legitimacy
Demands a $5,500 fee to release a delayed courier package
Son reports the scam to police but the mother ignores it

snippet: A mother's romance with a supposed military sergeant led her to set up a business and bank account to receive funds. Her son found a fake courier receipt and photos on a scam-watch page, but she still believes the sergeant is real.

events.detail: Offers pay to rent out a freelancing account
Sends a polished contractor agreement to seem safe

snippet: A warning describes job offers that pay people to rent out their freelancing accounts, which are used to launder stolen funds. It explains the bans, liability and steps to take.

events.detail: Recorded voicemail from a tax relief group calls from changing numbers
Says collections continue unless the victim responds promptly
Asks how to stop repeated calls after opting out

snippet: A taxpayer who already filed keeps receiving robocalls from changing numbers offering to settle tax debt for pennies. They asked how to stop the calls.

events.detail: Attorneys general send a notice citing thousands of traceback alerts

snippet: A research report argues a telecom subsidiary enabled a large share of imposter robocalls, citing regulator notices. The report names the company's US units as the main enablers.

events.detail: Text offers part-time online job earning up to $6,000 monthly
Work account shows a growing balance and commission earnings
Funds negative account balances to keep completing tasks
Demands large withdrawal fees and fake IRS and guarantee letters
Secret Service traces transfers abroad but cannot recover funds

snippet: A victim was lured by a text offering online product-rating work and shown a large fake balance. They say about $350,000 of their own and others' money went into fees, and authorities could not recover the transfers.

events.detail: YouTube ads show a fake charity appeal for an at-risk person

snippet: A viewer found ads asking for donations for a supposedly vulnerable individual, with the funds going to an unrelated religious organization. The viewer believes the cases are fabricated.

events.detail: Tax office calls saying the victim dropped off extra income paperwork
Forged 1099 form submitted to add $72,500 of income
Calls the insurer, finds no record and stops the filing

snippet: A taxpayer was called by a tax office claiming they had dropped off a forged 1099 for large extra income. They checked with the insurer, found no record and stopped the filing.

events.detail: Voicemail claims account was flagged and asks for a callback
Blocks the number and marks the message as spam

snippet: A person received a voicemail claiming their tax file needed review and asked for a callback. They blocked the number and marked the message as spam.

events.detail: Homeowners pay upfront and then see no progress on work
Federal court convicts contractor over fake tax records scheme

snippet: A warning describes a remodeling contractor with unresolved complaints from customers who paid for unfinished work. Federal court records also describe a fraud case involving fake tax records.

events.detail: Sends extensive business and personal documents to the accountant
Notes repeated missed calls and cancelled video meetings

snippet: A foreign business owner sent sensitive personal and business information to a CPA they found through a government list. They grew suspicious after repeated missed calls and cancelled meetings.

events.detail: Dishonest preparer reports a phantom business loss for a large refund

snippet: An accountant warns that dishonest tax preparers can add phantom business losses to inflate refunds. Taxpayers remain liable for back taxes even if they were unaware.

events.detail: Robocall impersonating the IRS answered by mistake
Hangs up and blocks the number

snippet: A person gets frequent scam calls, and one IRS-themed call reached them. They hung up, blocked the number and asked how to stop the calls.

events.detail: Voicemail claims an account review needs a callback
Doubts the call because the IRS usually writes by mail

snippet: A person who had already filed received a voicemail claiming their account was under review and asking for a callback. They doubted it because the IRS usually contacts people by mail.

events.detail: Repeated voicemails claim a tax matter is headed to collections
Reports spam and deletes each voicemail

snippet: A person has received the same IRS-themed voicemail for over a month from different numbers. They report and delete each one and asked whether there is a way to stop them.

events.detail: Robo voicemails claim a special IRS tax resolution unit
Calls back the numbers and asks for the caller's name

snippet: A person receives many voicemails claiming to be from an IRS tax resolution unit. They started calling back, asking for names, and wanted to warn others.

events.detail: Spoofed IRS-style email asks to review a reconciliation document
Does not open the download after browser flags a virus

snippet: A taxpayer received a spoofed email asking them to review a reconciliation document after their refund was approved. They did not open the file and confirmed the IRS does not request this by email.

events.detail: Stranger sends a Zelle payment with no explanation
Asks whether the transfers could be used to access the account

snippet: A friend received a Zelle payment from a stranger, then a larger one a month later with no contact. The friend asks whether these transfers could be a scam to gain account access.

events.detail: Real estate firm job offer with unusually high entry-level pay
Sends a $4,300 check to buy specialised equipment
Sends $500 by Zelle toward the equipment
Realises the check failed and contacts the bank

snippet: A job applicant was sent a $4,300 check to buy equipment for a fake real estate job. They sent $500 by Zelle, then the check failed and the applicant contacted their bank.

events.detail: Caller claims to be a bank about suspicious Zelle transfers
Transfers caller to a fake returns department
Hangs up and calls the bank's official number

snippet: A bank customer received a call about two suspicious Zelle transfers and was passed to a fake returns department. They hung up, called the number on their card and confirmed it was a scam.

events.detail: Crypto P2P buyer pays through several third-party Zelle transfers
Callers demand the seller return the money
Suspects a triangulation scam after releasing the crypto

snippet: A crypto seller received several Zelle payments from different people for one sale and was later asked to refund them. The seller suspects a triangulation scam and asks how banks handled similar cases.

events.detail: Client requests a logo design and offers payment only by check
Suspects an overpayment and refund check scam

snippet: A freelance logo designer was contacted through a website form for a project paid only by check. The designer was suspicious of the check-only request and asked whether it was an overpayment scam.

events.detail: Fake salvage yard contacted buyer on WhatsApp after a search
Buyer paid for a wheel via Zelle and never received it
Fake courier demanded a refundable $120 insurance fee
Buyer recognised the insurance demand as the final sign of fraud
Buyer refused to pay the courier fee
Buyer realised the wheel payment was gone

snippet: A buyer paid a fake salvage yard for a wheel and never received it. The fake courier then demanded an insurance fee, which the buyer refused to pay.

events.detail: Stranger sent $500 via Zelle and said it was a mistake
Bank fraud agent advised the recipient to send the money back personally
Recipient recognised a payment reversal scam pattern
Recipient refused to send the money back

snippet: A person received an unexpected $500 transfer and was told by a bank agent to send it back. They refused, recognising a common payment reversal scam.

events.detail: Broker quoted a reasonable price using a legitimate company's reputation
Customer paid the initial moving quote by credit card
Movers claimed extra cubic feet and demanded more money
Customer paid an extra $2,000 via Zelle under pressure
Belongings held in storage until an outstanding balance was paid
Customer found the company unreachable and delivery dates shifting

snippet: A family hired a moving broker and was pressured into paying an extra $2,000. Their belongings were then held in storage until a further balance was demanded.

events.detail: Call showed a major bank name on the caller ID
Caller posed as bank fraud department about Zelle payments
Caller demanded quick action to stop payments before they went through
Recipient checked the apps and saw no such transactions
Recipient hung up and planned to call the bank directly

snippet: A caller posing as a bank fraud team claimed two Zelle payments needed urgent cancellation. The recipient found no such transactions and hung up.

events.detail: Facebook seller said item was dropped with a courier quickly
Buyer paid $110 via Zelle for a motorcycle part
Fake logistics firm demanded $170 international transit insurance
Buyer questioned an insurance fee for a domestic shipment

snippet: A buyer paid a Facebook seller for a motorcycle part and was then asked for an insurance fee by a logistics firm. The buyer suspected both were part of a scam.

events.detail: Caller claimed to be from a bank about a $900 charge
Caller transferred target to a fake Zelle fraud department
Representative insisted disputes be filed immediately or charges are final
Target realised the caller was not from the bank
Target refused to share balance details and hung up

snippet: A caller posing as a bank asked about fraudulent charges and transferred the target to a fake Zelle team. The target refused to share balance details and hung up.

events.detail: Call claimed to be from a bank the target does not use
Caller transferred target to a fake Zelle representative
Target reported the call to their real bank as a scam
Target ended the call without taking any action

snippet: A caller posing as a bank transferred the target to a fake Zelle representative who claimed to cancel transfers. The target reported it to their real bank and lost nothing.

events.detail: Buyer asked to ship an item out of state and paid $220
Buyer asked to text the seller and use a different address
Seller doubts the buyer's requests and suspects a scam

snippet: A seller received an out-of-state buyer who asked for a changed shipping address and to communicate by text. The seller began to suspect the sale was a scam.

events.detail: Buyer offered to pay in advance for a $175 desk
Fake Zelle support contact demanded a $500 minimum transfer
Seller noticed red flags and reported the buyer as a scam
Seller stopped engaging and sent no money

snippet: A seller was approached by a buyer who offered to pay in advance and then sent a fake Zelle support contact. The seller reported the buyer and sent no money.

events.detail: Realtor approved an application and sent a lease and receipt
Realtor claimed to represent a registered rental company
Payment requests moved to different payees and then to CashApp
Applicant noticed payee names differed from the landlord
Applicant did not send money and planned to question the realtor

snippet: An applicant was asked to pay rent and deposit into several differently named accounts and then through CashApp. The applicant stopped before sending any money.

events.detail: Rogue transfers left her account for unknown recipients
Bank and payment apps each said responsibility lay elsewhere

snippet: A person's relative saw money leave her account through transfers she did not make. Her bank and payment apps each said the responsibility lay with someone else.

events.detail: Caller claimed to be from a bank about a suspicious transaction
Caller verified identity while relaying answers to the real bank
Victim gave card number, SSN and date of birth
Victim read back one-time verification codes to the caller
Victim realised the call was wrong and phoned family
Family and bank fraud team froze accounts and confirmed no loss

snippet: A caller posing as a bank obtained personal details and verification codes from an older victim while relaying them to the real bank. Family and the bank fraud team froze the accounts and confirmed no money had left.

events.detail: Buyer offered $50 for a $35 item and offered to cover shipping
Buyer repeatedly pushed to reserve and pay before shipping
Seller found the overpayment and shipping offer suspicious

snippet: A seller received an offer above the asking price with shipping covered, and the buyer pressed for payment before shipping. The seller grew suspicious and asked how to stay safe.

events.detail: Parent emailed a tutor about sessions for a child abroad
Conversation moved from email to text messages
Tutor noticed unclear English and odd payment instructions
Tutor did not proceed with the mobile check arrangement

snippet: A tutor was contacted by a parent offering to pay by emailed mobile check. The tutor noticed the red flags and did not proceed.

events.detail: Buyer comments on a listing and leaves a phone number
Buyer moves to phone contact and says a relative will collect
Fake screenshots claim an overpayment sent as a business transaction
Scammers become aggressive when the seller does not comply

snippet: A seller describes buyers who comment on listings, move the conversation to a phone number, and send fake screenshots of an overpayment. They become aggressive when the seller does not comply.

events.detail: Friend asked the victim to receive a buyer's payment for a clothing sale
Victim forwarded $700 received from the buyer via Cash App
Bank put the account on hold and opened no fraud case
Victim learned the buyer had been scammed and contacted the bank

snippet: A person agreed to receive and forward a $700 payment for a friend's clothing sale, and later learned the buyer had been scammed. The bank then placed the person's account on hold.

events.detail: Landlord gave a relative's payment app for a $500 deposit
Payment app blocked the transfer and warned it was likely a scam
Renter asked for buyer-protected payment and was refused

snippet: A renter was asked to pay a $500 deposit through a relative's payment app, which the app blocked as a likely scam. The landlord refused a protected payment method.

events.detail: Unknown number sent $2,500 via Zelle and texted it was a mistake
Texts demanded the money be returned immediately
Bank advised leaving the money in place for reversal
Parent suspected fraud and blocked the number

snippet: A teenager received a $2,500 Zelle transfer from an unknown number, followed by texts demanding its return. The parent blocked the number and the money was left in the account.

events.detail: Facebook precious metals business had months of activity and reviews
Buyer paid via Zelle for a precious metals purchase
Business account was deleted with no communication after four days

snippet: A buyer paid a Facebook precious metals business through Zelle and then heard nothing. The business account was deleted, and the buyer filed disputes and an IC3 complaint.

events.detail: Artist contacted victim on a music platform offering a split
Scammer's social media accounts looked legitimate to the victim
Sent checks as payment for the painting project
Pressured victim to pay a paint supplier quickly
Victim paid about $1,000 via Zelle and Apple Pay
Bank froze the account and the payments were gone

snippet: A person recruited as an artist received checks and was pressured into paying a supplier about $1,000 through Zelle and Apple Pay. The bank then froze the account and the money was lost.

events.detail: Call came from a real bank phone number about new Zelle payments
Caller claimed to be bank fraud prevention needing Zelle cancellation
Caller said action had to happen immediately or funds could not be stopped
Victim questioned the free email address used for the reference
Victim hung up and phoned the bank directly

snippet: A caller posing as bank fraud prevention told the target to set up a Zelle cancellation. The target hung up and confirmed with the bank that no such call was made.

events.detail: Seller advertised concert tickets on TikTok with a phone number
Buyer sent the ticket payment via Cash App
Seller sent screen recording and tickets that appeared in Apple Wallet
Fake ticketing company emails said tickets would be cancelled unless fees paid
Buyer paid a $70 resale fee to keep the tickets
Seller demanded an additional $85 charge to return the tickets
Buyer asked for a refund and realised it was a scam
Refund never arrived because the seller's payment app blocked it

snippet: A buyer paid for concert tickets from a TikTok seller, then paid a fake resale fee after receiving realistic tickets and emails. The seller then demanded more money and blocked the buyer's refund.

events.detail: Google Maps listing directed victim to a Telegram booking
Booking conversation moved from the website to Telegram
Victim paid a deposit to a Chime account
Sent a fake appointment confirmation screenshot
Victim found the address was an alley next to a hotel
Telegram messages were edited to raise the required deposit
Victim sent further deposits after claimed double booking
Victim stopped after a $300 safety deposit was demanded

snippet: A person booked a massage through a fake Google Maps listing and paid several deposits to different Chime accounts. The amounts were edited upward in messages until the victim stopped.

events.detail: Buyer claimed to have paid, but payment showed as on hold
Fake Venmo support number sent via screenshot as a trusted contact
Victim shared screen on a FaceTime call with the caller
Victim realised the money was gone and the bank would not refund it

snippet: A marketplace seller was told a buyer's payment was on hold and was directed to a fake support line. The seller shared a screen with the scammer and lost money that the bank would not recover.

events.detail: Social media ad offered a free modeling audition for a child
Family paid a $50 refundable booking deposit
Salesperson pressured family to buy a $2,500 package on the spot
Family signed for and was charged a $2,500 portfolio package
Family felt uneasy and sent a cancellation email within two hours
Credit card issuer placed the charge on monitoring and advised a dispute

snippet: A family responded to a social media audition ad and was pressured into signing for a $2,500 modeling package. They cancelled quickly and disputed the charge with their card issuer.

events.detail: Call spoofed a bank number with poor audio quality
Caller claimed fraudulent charges and walked through a Zelle transfer
Victim recognised the transfer to self as obviously a scam
Victim hung up and ignored repeated calls
Bank changed passwords and cards after the victim reported it

snippet: A caller posing as a bank tried to walk the target through sending their savings to a Zelle account. The target hung up, and the bank reset the account credentials and cards.

events.detail: Investment Discord linked from a trading forum was used as a lure
Live stock calls and vouching members built credibility in the group
Victim was directed to a fake copy-trading platform
Victim deposited $3,000 via PayPal to the platform
Victim deposited $2,500 via Venmo and $500 via Zelle
Host aggressively pressured the victim to deposit more
Victim realised the platform was fake and members were bots
PayPal and Venmo refunded, but the bank denied the $500 Zelle refund

snippet: A person was lured into a fake copy-trading platform through a Discord group and deposited $6,000. Payment providers refunded most of it, but the $500 Zelle deposit was not recovered.

events.detail: Buyer asked for Zelle or Venmo details before viewing the TV
Buyer followed up by email with a link to a website
Victim entered debit card details on the fake receiving site
Victim uploaded an ID and face photos for verification
Victim's account was drained, leaving only $1

snippet: A seller of a TV was tricked into sharing debit card details, ID and face photos through a fake website. The seller's account was drained by about $1,000.

events.detail: Fake rental listing booked a tour that gave a temporary door code
Scammer had the victim sign a fake rental contract
Victim paid $2,600 through a payment app to the fake landlord
Victim could not recover the payment after realising the scam

snippet: A renter was shown a rental property through a temporary access code and signed a fake contract. The renter paid $2,600 through a payment app and could not get it back.

events.detail: Buyer reacted quickly to a listing and asked general questions
Buyer gave a number to message off Facebook
Buyer asked to pay first via Zelle or a cash app
Seller refused to sign up for a payment app and sent no money

snippet: A Facebook Marketplace seller was approached by a buyer who wanted to move off-platform and pay first through Zelle or a cash app. The seller refused and lost nothing.

events.detail: Victim joined a Discord trading server run by a self-described options trader
Host had made good calls that day, building credibility
Victim sent $2,700 in USDC on promise of a Zelle return
Host kept asking for more money when the victim asked for repayment
Victim never got the funds back and was removed from the server

snippet: A person was persuaded by a Discord options host to send $2,700 in USDC on a promised return. When they asked for their money back the host demanded more and removed them from the server.

events.detail: Membership club offered introductions to women for a fee
Match sent only library photos and never a live selfie
Repeated new fees and deposits were required before any date
Target asked for a live selfie and challenged the match's reality
Target blocked the match and never sent money

snippet: A man was pulled into a paid dating club that asked for repeated fees before a date. He refused to pay further, questioned the match's identity, and blocked her.

events.detail: Client commissioned an artwork and offered a check
Sent a check for twice the agreed commission amount
Artist realised she was expected to refund the excess payment

snippet: An artist received a commission check for twice the agreed amount and was asked to refund the difference. The artist deposited the check and refused to send the money back.

events.detail: Buyer asked seller to text their wife instead of the app
Conversation moved from the marketplace to text messages
Fake Zelle agent said the seller's account was a business account
Seller shared screen on a FaceTime call and was asked to send $499
Seller felt uneasy and asked for a supervisor
Seller refused to complete the transaction and stopped

snippet: A seller of leather seats was moved to text and then asked to share a screen and send $499 to unlock a payment. The seller refused, and the bank stopped the transaction.

events.detail: Woman at a gas station asked for help paying for fuel
Driver later realised the request was a scam
Driver refused to pay and did not hand over money

snippet: A driver at a gas station was asked for help paying for fuel in exchange for foreign currency. The driver refused and did not give any money.

events.detail: Two men in a pickup told the driver her license plate had fallen off
Driver recognised her plate number and sensed danger
Driver kept driving and did not pull over

snippet: A driver was approached by men in a pickup who claimed her license plate had fallen off and held up a different plate. She recognised the plate was not hers, kept driving, and called for help.

events.detail: Buyer replied to a camera listing with an overseas deployment story
Buyer claimed military service and offered PayPal payment
Seller said the camera was sold and sent no details

snippet: A seller received an inquiry from a buyer claiming to be a deployed soldier who wanted a gift shipped. The seller did not send any payment details or the item.

events.detail: Free business presentation with big-name speakers pitched a course
Victim bought a $6,000 real estate course at the presentation
Victim returned the course and lost only the shipping cost

snippet: A person attended a free business presentation and bought a $6,000 real estate course. They returned it and lost only the cost of shipping it back.

events.detail: Unknown company repeatedly called claiming an unpaid balance
Company mailed a semi-legitimate looking bill for non-payment
Police and post office found no trace of the company
Recipient could not verify the company or the debt

snippet: A person received repeated calls and a fake-looking bill from a company they had never heard of, claiming an unpaid balance. Police and the post office could not trace the company, and the person paid nothing.

events.detail: Photo company sends a packet home and demands payment
Teacher blocks a field trip unless payment is brought in
Parent cites a state statute saying payment demands are illegal

snippet: A parent says a school photo company sends pictures home and demands payment, and a teacher has threatened a child with missing a field trip. The parent refuses to pay and cites a state statute.

events.detail: Man offered to donate a classic car to a charity for a raffle
Pushed the charity to start raffle and hand over a check quickly
Volunteer found the car title showed a 1980 reproduction
Board agreed the deal was a bad idea and declined

snippet: A man offered a charity a car to raffle off in exchange for a $30,000 advance check. A volunteer uncovered the car's age and the man's record, and the board declined.

events.detail: Moving company quoted $3,200 and then subcontracted the haul
Driver demanded $6,800 before delivering the household goods
Driver insisted on payment in cash or money order
Customers contacted the company over 50 times with no real answers

snippet: A family hired a moving company that subcontracted the job, and the driver demanded $6,800 in cash before delivering their furniture. The family could not get straight answers from the company.

events.detail: Near-daily texts from UK numbers reading only 2018
Recipient never replied and cannot block the changing numbers

snippet: A person in Ireland receives near-daily texts from changing UK numbers that only say 2018. The recipient has never replied and has lost nothing.

events.detail: Celebrities promoted crypto offerings without disclosing paid endorsements
Securities regulator charged the promoters with fraud

snippet: Two celebrities promoted cryptocurrency coin offerings without disclosing they had been paid. A securities regulator charged them with fraud.

events.detail: Phone call claimed Visa or MasterCard offered 0% interest
Caller claimed a business relationship between card networks and banks
Listener asked for their name and the caller swore
Listener ended the call and shared no information

snippet: A person received a call claiming their card company was offering 0% interest. When they asked the caller for their name, the caller cursed and hung up.

events.detail: Voicemail with a Texas area code claimed to be from the IRS
Caller claimed an arrest warrant for fraudulent tax filing
Caller repeatedly demanded the Social Security number and name
Recipient called back on a blocked line and recognised the script

snippet: A person received a voicemail from someone claiming to be the IRS and threatening an arrest warrant. The person called back, recognised the script, and did not share any details.

events.detail: Caller posed as a mail prescription service
Caller asked to verify the card used for prescription deliveries
Recipient stalled the caller with false details and hung up

snippet: A caller posing as a prescription mail service asked for a credit card number. The recipient stalled with invented prescriptions and ended the call without giving any details.

events.detail: Caller phoned about the recipient's computer
Second caller claimed to be from Microsoft technical department
Recipient mocked the call and recognised the search-result trick

snippet: A caller claimed to be from Microsoft about an infected computer and read out a serial number. The recipient exposed the trick by pointing out it was an easy web search result.

events.detail: Shop ran ads encouraging bulk purchases of discounted items
About-us photo of the owner was taken from another person's site

snippet: A shop posing as a small handmade craft business sold dropshipped goods. Its owner photo was taken from another person's website.

events.detail: Late-night caller claimed to be from a bank about a transfer
Caller asked for social security number and account details to verify
Spouse called official bank lines to check the calls
Bank helplines said the calls were genuine, but branch manager disagreed

snippet: A spouse received calls claiming to be from a bank asking for personal and account details. Bank helplines said the calls were genuine, but a branch manager later called the requests extremely sketchy.

events.detail: Promoter event pitched a crypto investment to an audience of novices
BBC investigated and Rwanda issued warnings against the scheme

snippet: A photographer observed a promotion event pitching a crypto investment to an audience with little financial knowledge. The scheme has since been investigated by the BBC and warned against by Rwanda.

events.detail: Recruiter contacted applicant over messaging after a job application
Claimed to be a staffing firm offering a remote job
Sent a check from an unrelated company for equipment purchase
Trainer pressed the applicant to deposit the check immediately
Applicant called the named company and confirmed the check was fake
Police and the FBI were contacted about the fraud

snippet: An applicant received a remote job offer and a check for equipment from a fake recruiter. The applicant verified with the named company, did not deposit the check, and reported the fraud.

events.detail: Puppy seller replied to dog ads with a sad backstory
Conversation moved from the website to email
Victim gave name, address and phone number to the seller
Victim searched online and found similar scams

snippet: A buyer responded to puppy ads and shared personal details with a seller who asked for an address and phone number. The buyer sent no money and became suspicious after searching online.

events.detail: Payer sent $150 via PayPal then said it was a mistake
Repeated money requests demanded a refund to the payer
Recipient suspected a hacked account and bounced payment
PayPal refused to reverse the transaction

snippet: A content creator received a $150 PayPal payment and was then repeatedly asked to send it back as a mistake. PayPal refused to reverse the payment, and the recipient feared a bounced transfer.

events.detail: Automated voicemail about a federal criminal offense
Message claimed a grand jury issue and a federal agent
Message called itself a final attempt to resolve the issue
Recipient ignored the voicemail and did not call back

snippet: A person received an automated voicemail claiming a federal criminal matter and urging a call back. They did not return the call.

events.detail: Wrong number reached a line mimicking a card company greeting
Recording offered an optional too-good-to-be-true card offer
Caller realised the number was one digit off the real line

snippet: A caller dialled a number one digit off a card company and heard a recording pitching an offer. The caller hung up, having given no information.

events.detail: Fake realty company emailed claiming to have taken over management
Email attached welcome letters to make the takeover look legitimate
Tenant texted the real landlord, who confirmed it was a scam
Landlord confirmed management was not changing and no portal was needed

snippet: A tenant received an email from a fake realty company claiming their building was under new management and asking them to log in to a new portal. The tenant checked with the landlord, who confirmed it was a scam, and nothing was lost.

events.detail: Buyer texted a seller asking to verify with a code
Seller recognised the verification code request as a scam pattern
Seller refused to call or share a verification code

snippet: A seller was contacted by a buyer who wanted a phone verification code to set up accounts. The seller recognised the scam pattern and refused to share the code.

events.detail: Text from a fake phone provider claimed a problem with the bill
Lookalike provider site asked for login and then debit card details
Partner entered email and password on the lookalike site
Partner checked the real account on a PC and stopped

snippet: A person received a text claiming a phone bill problem and entered login details on a lookalike provider site. They stopped before entering card details after checking the real account and found all bills paid.

events.detail: Post questions whether scammers use bad spelling to filter victims

snippet: A poster questions the common claim that scammers write poorly on purpose to filter out savvy targets. The post describes no specific scam event.

events.detail: Craigslist roommate ad drew a call and an in-person visit
Handed over keys and showed the room to seem like a real landlord
Victim paid $800 by money order for rent and deposit
Actual occupant revealed the house was used as an Airbnb
Victim lost the $800 and police called it a civil matter

snippet: A person paid $800 by money order for a room after being shown a house and given keys. The renter learned it was not the scammer's property and police treated the matter as civil.

events.detail: Noticed alerts for large packages never ordered
Found fraudulent card and address on credit report
Retailer and bank confirmed fraud and opened investigation

snippet: A person received many unordered packages after a fraudster opened a credit card in their name. They reported the fraud to the retailer and bank and froze their credit.

events.detail: Driver asked rider to cancel the order so he could collect a fee
Rider refused to cancel and asked driver to do it

snippet: A ride-hailing driver asked a passenger to cancel an order, which could have triggered a cancellation fee. The passenger refused and the scheme did not work.
